Norwegian:
Ved tidens start, var ett fundament.
Én enkelt blokk, uten rammer, helt allpotent.
I tomrommet den sto,
den slo seg til ro,
En tilfreds blokk som kjerneelement.

Verden vokste, hver generasjon var frekvent.
Strømmer av liv, nydelig og eksellent.
Verdens natur,
Med intensjon om struktur,
Ble Kjerneblokkens essens dens produsent.
English:
At the beginning of time, there was a foundation,
A single block, totally free with no limitation.
In an empty void,
It settled, overjoyed,
For what it just did, the Source block had started creation.

The world kept on growing with every generation.
And life kept on flowing, a beautiful sensation.
The nature of the world,
Intentions unfurled,
All essence of life flows out from the Source Block’s station.

Norwegian:
De elsket det vannet som sildret av sted,
Det brakte forsoning og ekte fred.
Åsene ble deres hjem,
samfunnet vokste frem.
Mens de nøt synet av strømmen, så mektig og vred.
English:
Some love the waters, rushing wildly unceased,
But still so serene, with tranquility and peace.
They claimed the hills,
And felt so fulfilled.
They admired the water, and then were pleased.

Norwegian:
De ville skue og beundre,
uten grunn til å dundre.
Her fantes ingen plikt,
som skapte konflikt,
De ville hvile, ikke plundre.
English:
They wanted no more than to sit and admire.
They just wanted peace, not even to inspire.
They wanted no work,
Nothing that could irk.
From anything strenuous, they wanted to retire.

Norwegian:
En leder av rang satt lunt i sin skygge,
Han gjorde det ulovelig å begynne å bygge.
«Ingen bygg skal være her!»
«Bygg er kun til vårt besvær!!»
«Foruten post, bro eller brygge.»
English:
Their leader was a man, who felt so fulfilled,
He made it illegal to begin any build.
“No build shall be here,”
“No build shall be there,”
“Unless it’s a lookout, or a bridge in the hills!”

Norwegian:
Han trengte ei noe høyt og flott,
Han ønsket seg ikke et langstragt slott.
Han tok allting med ro,
Lot behaget gro,
For målet om fred, det føltes godt.
English:
They didn’t need fancy or intricate things.
They didn’t need castles that were fit for a king.
Sit back and unwind,
And enjoy the good times.
They just wanted peace and nothing that stings.

Norwegian:
Men hvor er visjonen nå?
Det som startet så godt, kunne ei bestå,
Med null aktivitet,
Og en slapp mentalitet,
Måtte samfunnet til slutt forgå.
English:
But with all this inaction, how long could it last?
It started so good but was over quite fast.
With nothing to do,
And no goal to pursue,
They dwindled and became a culture of the past.

Norwegian:
Når verden er hard, så alle må streve,
kan motgang gi iver og kraft til å leve.
En flokk ville bo,
I ørkenens glo,
Et meningsfult liv å kreve.
English:
When the climate is harsh and you need to survive,
It gives you passion, and it gives you a drive.
A group put in effort,
To live in the desert,
And after a while, they learned how to thrive.

Norwegian:
De levde forsonlig og bygde med klang.
På tross av hardt klima, de skrattet og sang.
«Her vil vi bli,»
«Nå er vi på gli!»
For gleden var større enn livets gang.
English:
They lived in great peace and built some great things.
Despite the harsh climate, they would prosper and sing.
“Happy are we,”
“In the grainy sea!”
But could they face wealth, and whatever that brings?

Norwegian:
Han hadde en velstand som overgikk målet.
Og bygde et kammer der skatter fikk råde.
En leder så stor,
Vekket hatefulle ord.
Men suveren i sin makt, han fikk stråle.
English:
Their leader had greatness that no one could measure.
He made a great chamber and stored all his treasure.
A treasure so great,
It fostered some hate.
Knowing he was peerless, that gave him great pleasure.

Norwegian:
Et marked av handel de sprengte.
Alt kostet, selv det de trengte.
Det ble en splittet stat,
Noen led åpent, andre privat.
I et hardt klima som fikk dem til å lengte.
English:
In this culture they had wealth and items they would trade.
Not a thing there was free, not even imperative aid.
This made a divide.
Some rose and some cried.
The climate was harsh, and there was no shade.

Norwegian:
Lederen var en grusom blokk.
Men folket var sinte, de hadde fått nok.
«Slutt å plyndre oss!»
«Nå vil vi ut og sloss!»
Det som startet så flott, endte i et sjokk.
English:
The leader was cruel, he was nothing but tough.
But the people hit their limit, they had been through enough.
“We won’t take it anymore!”
“We are going to war!”
It started with greatness, but the ending was rough.

Norwegian:
I landet mot nord, der vinden er kald,
lå isen begravd under snøens lette fall.
Noen fant stor prakt,
og inngikk en pakt,
Om å slå seg ned i vinterens hall.
English:
In the cold winter’s land, in the freezing breeze,
Where the snow floats around and the ice is at ease,
Some people found beauty,
And made it their duty,
To live in this place where the frost doesn’t cease.

Norwegian:
De elsket alt som glitret,
Med et håp og en drøm som sitret.
«Jeg vil bli vakker,»
«Slik som landets bakker.»
Og med ett var folket smigret.
English:
They loved how the ground just glittered and gleamed.
With a glimmer of hope, they yearned and they dreamed.
“My looks should be grand,”
“Akin to this land.”
They valued great beauty, so their customs were themed.

Norwegian:
En leder ble valgt, hun var skjønn og så pen.
På en skala til hundre, var hun hundre og én.
Hennes blokk var perfekt,
De falt om i affekt.
Hun steg frem som et nytt fenomen.
English:
A leader was chosen, her beauty was great,
On a scale up to six, her level was eight.
So fine was her block,
It often sparked shock.
But was that enough to lead people’s fate?

Norwegian:
Deres leder var vakker, og folket var glad,
Men evnen til å lede var slett ikke bra.
Hun var alltid i tvil,
Og fikk sjeldent en hvil.
For hun tok ingen valg og sa aldri fra.
English:
The leader was pretty, her people were glad,
But frankly her skills as a leader were bad.
She was very unsure,
And quite insecure.
She couldn’t make choices, they just made her sad.

Norwegian:
Det gikk som det måtte med henne som leder.
Det ble slett ingen fremgang på diverse steder.
Motivasjonen stoppet,
Og samfunnet floppet,
Da folket mistet sine gleder.
English:
So how could it work, with such a bad leader?
Well nothing got better, and nothing got neater.
Motivation stopped flowing.
They couldn’t keep going.
They lost all their drive, and they fell from their teeter.

Norwegian:
Dypt under bakken ved et flammende fjell,
Lå små grotter med brennende sprell.
En liten gjeng sanset,
Mens lavaen danset,
Noe i veggen med storslått appell.
English:
Deep in the caves, with rivers of fire,
Where elevation is lower, and temperature higher,
A small group did settle.
By the fire’s cettle,
They found in the walls a gorgeous desire.

Norwegian:
De satte opp gruver, der gikk de berserk.
De knuste vekk blokker og bygde sine verk.
Men med tiden der inne,
Fikk tankene spinne.
De dro dit hvor solen sto sterk.
English:
They broke down the caves and set up their mines.
They mined many blocks and built some long lines.
But they missed the outside,
So they had to decide,
To bring all their things and go where sun shines.

Norwegian:
En dag kom en dame som var helt bekvem.
Hun svingte seg over kløfter og fant veien frem.
Dette var stedet
hvor hun bygde sitt rede.
En smie hun kalte sitt hjem.
English:
Someday a woman found joy in the deep.
She swung across chasms and ravines that were steep.
This was the place,
Where she set up her base.
She built a great forge and called it her keep.

Norwegian:
En smie ble bygd i de dypeste huler,
Den knuste blokker og slukte dem som smuler.
De ble smeltet til en pytt,
Og ut kom noe nytt,
Metall formet som blokker og moduler.
English:
In the fiery caves, a forge was erected.
It needed to be fueled, many blocks were collected.
It turned them askew,
And made something new.
It ate many blocks and metal was ejected.

Norwegian:
Smien gjorde sin nytte med voldsom energi,
Men så kom det en mann, og damen sluttet å smi.
Han ble hennes nye flamme,
Og de ble aldri de samme.
Da hun slo seg til ro med en ny filosofi.
English:
She built something grand, a forge with great force,
But soon someone came and altered her course.
She encountered a man,
Who changed her plan.
She abandoned the forge and settled with remorse.

Norwegian:
Blant sumpenes myrer og skogkledde hager,
De med vidunderlig vakre og magiske blader,
Oppsto et samfunn,
Fra ulik bakgrunn,
Med stadig mindre og større tirader.
English:
In the marshes of the swamp, in the cluster of trees,
With wonderful, beautiful and magical leaves,
A society had formed.
Together, they felt warm.
But how long can it last when no one agrees?

Norwegian:
De var ikke mange, de var ganske få.
Men viljen var sterk og lidenskapen rå.
De elsket og jamret
mens hjertene hamret.
Nåden ga livet et nytt nivå.
English:
There were not many people who lived in this place,
But their spirit was strong, and their anger gave chase.
They would love and adore,
And be furious to the core.
They lived happily here with passion and grace.

Norwegian:
Men alt gikk på tverke da en jente fant sopp,
En med vidunderlig vakker og magisk kropp.
Hun var stolt og kry,
Men den ble snart til bry.
Da livet hun kjente snart sa stopp.
English:
But everything changed when a girl found a mushroom,
With a wonderful, beautiful and magical fume.
This made her glad,
But soon, she’d be sad.
She wasn’t aware this would end with a boom.

Norwegian:
Den magiske soppen gjorde så mangt.
Jenta brygget en drikk som lot henne gå langt.
Hun lot dem få smake,
Men det fantes en hake.
Et liv med bregrensninger var nå blitt for trangt.
English:
The magical mushroom granted her powers.
She made an elixir and walked on for hours.
She let people see,
But they could not agree.
Was it really that good, or was it just sour?

Norwegian:
Noen nektet å bruke det jenta hadde brakt,
Det med vidunderlig vakker og magisk prakt.
«Dette er viktig!»
«Vi må behandle soppen riktig!»
Det endte i jakt, der målet var slakt.
English:
Some thought it was wrong to use the small bell,
With a wonderful, beautiful and magical smell.
“This cannot be right!”
“We must stand and fight!”
It ended in war, and this society fell.

Norwegian:
Det er lett å drømme, men tungt å bevare.
Hvordan kan vi lære av fortidens snare?
Jeg vil møte hver en dag!
Jeg vil leve i behag!
Jeg vil se noe praktfullt jeg ikke kan forklare.
English:
It’s easy to dream, but can the dream last?
How can we change and learn from the past?
I want a new dawn!
I want to live on!
I want something great, I want something vast.

Norwegian:
Men hvordan kan jeg drømme når håpet er abstrakt?
Kan en blokk som meg oppnå en slik prakt?
Er det galt å sikte høyt?
Er det å drømme altfor drøyt?
Kan jeg likevel lykkes og lande intakt?
English:
But how can I dream with so little hope?
How can small blocks achieve such a scope?
Am I wrong to dream?
Going down the wrong stream?
How can I reach and not fall down a slope?

Norwegian:
Hvorfor er vi forhekset og dømt til å lide?
Begrensningene våre, de er morbide.
Hvorfor blir vi så trette,
hindret fra å ta oss til rette?
Når skal vi settes fri og få tid til å glide?
English:
Why do we suffer? Why are we cursed?
These limitations, they are the worst.
Why must we tire,
Not reach what we desire?
When can we be free? When can this bubble burst?

Norwegian:
Har naturen hat i sitt hjerte?
Har den alltid ønsket oss smerte?
Har jeg tatt feil i mitt sinn
og hele tiden vært blind?
Det må finnes noe mer, noe som er verdt det!
English:
Does nature itself have hatred in its heart?
Was it against us from the very start?
No, I must be blind,
To the reason behind.
There must be something more, there must be another part.

Norwegian:
Kanskje jeg kan lære å se skjønnhet der jeg går?
Kanskje er vi ment å verdsette det vi får?
Hva om vi forener våre talenter
og sammen bygger verdens senter?
Livet er kanskje kort, men det er nå jeg forstår.
English:
Maybe I must learn to see beauty where I’m at.
Maybe we’re meant to cherish every chat.
Maybe we’re meant for cooperation,
To build the world’s foundation.
Maybe life is short, and there’s beauty in that.
